openapiOps.summary: The observed verification verdict, not the configuration
openapiOps.description: Reports configuration completeness and, separately, whether a Bitcoin listing can actually be verified right now: storage writable, both nodes answering, and the ord index within its accepted lag of Bitcoin Core.

openapiOps.summary: The protocol contract this gateway speaks
The markets this gateway serves, and what it verifies for each
openapiOps.description: Every entry states its verification scope in plain language and its capabilities as booleans. An entry in the catalog never implies a working flow beyond what its capabilities state.

openapiOps.summary: One page of the orderbook
openapiOps.description: Paging is keyset, never offset. A request carrying an `offset` parameter is refused with 400, and a malformed cursor is a 400 rather than a silent restart from the first page.

parameters.name: protocols
parameters.description: Comma separated catalog ids. Applied before sorting and pagination.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: A catalog group id, expanded to every protocol it contains.

parameters.name: seller
parameters.description: Restricts the page to the listings one seller script owns.

parameters.name: assetInscriptionId
parameters.description: Restricts the page to orders claiming one inscription. Resolved through an index of order claims.

parameters.name: assetOutpoint
parameters.description: Restricts the page to orders claiming an asset at one `txid:vout`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Every sort ends on the order id, which is unique, so the ordering is total and a cursor resumes exactly. An unpriced order sorts after every priced one in both price directions.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size as a decimal string.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The keyset resume point a previous page answered with.

openapiOps.summary: The appended lifecycle log, newest first
openapiOps.description: Reads the appended transition log, so an entry is something that happened rather than a listing's current state restated after the fact.

openapiOps.summary: One order

200.description: The order, without its signed artifact.

openapiOps.summary: The signed artifact for one live listing
openapiOps.description: Deliberately its own rate limited request. A browse response carrying raw PSBTs would hand every public ask to anything that can read the market. Only a live listing hands over its artifact; any other state is refused with 400.

200.description: The signed artifact and its current verification.

openapiOps.summary: Take a signed artifact and verify it
openapiOps.description: A source may supply signed order evidence, but it never overrides what the node and the ord index prove. The claims travel as evidence and the authorities decide the state.

openapiOps.summary: Take a signed OpenOrdex event and verify it
openapiOps.description: Accepts a kind 802 Nostr event carrying a signed PSBT, verifies the event signature, then verifies the order exactly as a direct import.

openapiOps.summary: Build the unsigned seller half
openapiOps.description: Composes the one input, one output PSBT a seller signs `SIGHASH_SINGLE | SIGHASH_ANYONECANPAY`. The asset and outpoint are verified against the node and the ord index before anything is composed.

201.description: The unsigned seller half and its inspection.

openapiOps.summary: Take the signed seller half and publish it
The message a listing owner signs before managing it

200.description: The challenge to sign with the key that owns the offered output.

openapiOps.summary: Remove a listing, proved by the key owning the output it sells
openapiOps.description: Withdrawal is discovery, not cancellation. It stops this gateway publishing the listing; it cannot unpublish a signed artifact already distributed elsewhere. Only spending the offered output makes such an artifact unusable.

openapiOps.summary: Operator moderation, separately authenticated

401.description: Operator credentials missing, invalid, or not configured.

openapiOps.summary: The unsigned kind 802 event announcing this listing
openapiOps.description: The gateway never holds Nostr keys. The customer's own NIP-07 signer signs this envelope, the browser publishes it, and the signed event can then be handed back through the OpenOrdex import route.

openapiOps.summary: Recheck one order against both authorities

201.description: The order after a fresh verification.

openapiOps.summary: Compose the buyer half and state the exact terms
openapiOps.description: The caller names its own outputs and nothing else. Value and script are read from Bitcoin Core, never from the request, so a buyer cannot make a purchase look cheaper by describing their own funding wrongly. Each named output is checked against the ord index first: an output holding an asset is not spare change, and an unexamined output is unknown rather than empty.

201.description: The unsigned buyer half and the exact economics. A fee or a royalty of zero is stated as zero rather than omitted.

openapiOps.summary: Verify a signed purchase and ask the node whether it would accept it
openapiOps.description: Takes either `finalTxHex` or the `signedPsbt` a wallet actually answers with. Given a PSBT it finalises only inputs the buyer already signed: it creates no signature and changes no input, output, or amount, and an unsigned input is an error rather than a guess. It rechecks the order against the chain, binds the transaction to the order, proves the sat flow invariant, then asks the node itself. The gateway does not broadcast; that is the buyer's own deliberate step.

201.description: The verdict, with the exact bytes checked so a buyer broadcasts those and no others.

openapiOps.summary: Replace a live ask with a freshly signed one for the same output
openapiOps.description: Repricing is a protocol operation, not a database edit. The old order must be live, the owner proof must match the offered output, and the new artifact must be signed against the same outpoint. The old order leaves the book as REPLACED and the new one goes live in one step, and two live asks for one output and seller cannot exist.

201.description: The retired order id and the live replacement.

openapiOps.summary: Compose several live asks into one transaction
openapiOps.description: Up to eight asks, one funding plan, one transaction, composed only when every seller signature and every sat flow invariant can coexist. There is no partial composition: when any ask cannot be proved the answer names every refusal and settles nothing.

201.description: The composed batch with every placement stated.

409.description: At least one ask cannot coexist in the batch.

openapiOps.summary: Verify a signed batch and ask the node about the exact bytes
openapiOps.description: Rechecks every placement against both authorities, proves the sat flow invariant for every ask, then asks the node whether it would accept the composed transaction. The answer carries the exact bytes checked.

201.description: The per-ask verdicts and the node answer.

openapiOps.summary: One page of the offer book
openapiOps.description: Keyset paged exactly like the orders: limit and cursor in, nextCursor out, empty on the last page. A malformed cursor is a 400, never a silent first page.

openapiOps.summary: Publish a funded offer
openapiOps.description: Takes exact offer terms and funded-output evidence. The gateway recomputes the terms hash, recomputes the Taproot tree and tweak from the two leaves, requires the funded script to commit to both, asks Bitcoin Core whether the output exists and is unspent, and refuses everything else. The offer goes live once the funding confirms.

openapiOps.summary: One offer with its lifecycle state and freshness
Recheck one offer against both authorities
Remove an offer from discovery, proved by the recovery key
openapiOps.description: Discovery, not cancellation: the funded output stays spendable by the acceptance path until it is spent, and by the recovery path after expiry. A BIP 322 signature by the recovery key proves who may stop publishing the offer.

openapiOps.summary: State the exact acceptance arrangement for one live offer
openapiOps.description: Given the seller outpoint, reads every value from the node and the ord index, lays out padding, buyer asset, every preserve in sat order, the seller payment at the seller input index, and change, and refuses when the Feline is elsewhere, the root no longer holds, or expiry has passed.

201.description: The exact arrangement to build and sign.

openapiOps.summary: Verify a built acceptance and ask the node
openapiOps.description: Parses the complete acceptance, checks every rule in spec/offers.md including both policy signatures against the committed terms tree, then asks the node whether it would accept the bytes. The answer carries the exact bytes checked.

openapiOps.summary: Build a complete SafeOps plan
openapiOps.description: Resolves every selected outpoint against the protocol authorities, builds the deterministic output map and sat flow, and returns the full plan with its digest before any wallet opens. Unexamined inputs fail closed.

openapiOps.summary: One stored SafeOps plan
openapiOps.description: Returns the plan exactly as it was built, with its current actionability against the live chain.

parameters.name: planId
parameters.description: The plan identifier returned at creation.

openapiOps.summary: Refresh the execution shield for a plan
openapiOps.description: Re-reads every input, protocol ownership, mempool conflicts, and fee estimates, then either confirms the plan is still fresh or invalidates the signing session and names exactly what changed.

openapiOps.summary: Relay a fully signed transaction after an explicit user broadcast action
openapiOps.description: Verifies the signed result against its plan or manifest, runs Bitcoin Core preflight, and only then relays. The gateway never composes a signature and never broadcasts on its own initiative.

openapiOps.summary: Monitor one broadcast operation
openapiOps.description: Mempool state, conflicts, confirmations, replacement, and reorg reconciliation for one transaction, with the events that recorded every transition.

parameters.name: txid
parameters.description: The transaction id of the operation.

openapiOps.summary: Plan an RBF replacement of one of your transactions
openapiOps.description: Offered only when node policy allows the replacement and the user controls every required input. Asset outputs, third party payments, and seller outputs are preserved; the extra fee comes only from user owned cardinal value.

openapiOps.summary: Plan a CPFP child for one of your stuck transactions
openapiOps.description: Offered only when the user controls a spendable output whose spending moves no tracked asset. The child fee is computed from the combined package fee rate under node package policy.

openapiOps.summary: Publish a signed swap intent
openapiOps.description: Verifies the BIP-322 maker proof, the intent digest, and the current state of every committed outpoint before the intent goes live. Private intents are never listed publicly.

openapiOps.summary: List live public swap intents
openapiOps.description: Keyset pagination by creation. Every intent is returned with the gateway independent resolution of its committed outpoints.

openapiOps.summary: One swap intent with its live outpoint state
openapiOps.description: The taker view independently resolves every asset claim against the chain authorities instead of repeating the maker text.

openapiOps.summary: Withdraw a swap intent
openapiOps.description: Only the maker may withdraw, proven by a fresh BIP-322 signature over the withdrawal request.

openapiOps.summary: Build the one transaction acceptance plan for a taker
openapiOps.description: Revalidates the maker outpoints, resolves the taker selection, builds exact input order for sat flow safety, assigns fees only to permitted cardinal value, and refuses any combination that cannot settle in one transaction.

openapiOps.summary: One swap session with its signature progress
openapiOps.description: Shows which party has signed, the current outpoint and conflict state, and whether the session is ready for preflight or broadcast.

openapiOps.summary: Submit one party signed PSBT
openapiOps.description: The submitted PSBT is compared against the acceptance plan. An input added, removed, reordered, or re signed outside the policy refuses the submission.

openapiOps.summary: Run node preflight on the fully signed swap
openapiOps.description: Only a transaction carrying every required signature reaches this route. Bitcoin Core testmempoolaccept decides.

openapiOps.summary: Relay the fully signed swap after the explicit user broadcast action
openapiOps.description: Both parties assets move in one transaction or not at all. The relay happens only after the user action and a passing preflight.

openapiOps.summary: Store an encrypted private swap link
openapiOps.description: The payload is encrypted client side. The server stores ciphertext and routing metadata only, never the key, never the terms, never a log of either.

openapiOps.summary: List the caller stored private swap envelopes
openapiOps.description: Returns ciphertext envelopes only. Decryption happens client side with the key from the URL fragment.

openapiOps.summary: Fetch one encrypted private swap envelope
openapiOps.description: Returns the ciphertext. The decryption key lives in the URL fragment and is never sent to the server.

openapiOps.summary: Destroy an encrypted private swap envelope
openapiOps.description: Client side destruction: the ciphertext is removed and the envelope is marked destroyed.

openapiOps.summary: Keyset paginated event history
openapiOps.description: Replay by cursor. Seven days minimum retention. Reversals appear as reverted events naming the event they reverse.

openapiOps.summary: Server sent event stream of live events
openapiOps.description: Filter by network, event type, aggregate, protocol, or collection. Last-Event-ID resumption, heartbeats, bounded buffers, and slow consumer disconnection with a resumable cursor. The same envelopes are available over WebSocket at the streaming gateway.

200.description: An SSE stream of ordex-event/v1 envelopes with id, event, and data fields.

openapiOps.summary: The current stream sequence and lag
openapiOps.description: Lets a consumer decide whether it is behind and from which cursor to resume without gaps.

openapiOps.summary: Create a webhook subscription
openapiOps.description: Returns the signing secret exactly once. The endpoint stays PENDING_VERIFICATION until it answers the challenge.

201.description: The subscription with its one time secret.

openapiOps.summary: List your webhook subscriptions
openapiOps.description: Bound to the authenticated developer key.

openapiOps.summary: One webhook subscription
openapiOps.description: Never returns the signing secret.

openapiOps.summary: Update, pause, or resume a subscription
openapiOps.description: URL changes re-enter verification.

openapiOps.summary: Delete a webhook subscription
openapiOps.description: Pending deliveries drain before removal.

openapiOps.summary: Rotate the signing secret
openapiOps.description: The old secret keeps verifying during a bounded overlap window so rotation never drops a delivery.

openapiOps.summary: Answer the endpoint challenge
openapiOps.description: The endpoint must echo the challenge value delivered to it before the subscription activates.

openapiOps.summary: Send a signed test delivery
openapiOps.description: A ping envelope signed exactly like a real delivery.

openapiOps.summary: Delivery history with attempt detail
openapiOps.description: Keyset paginated, filterable by subscription and state.

openapiOps.summary: Replay one delivery
openapiOps.description: Re-signs the original body and re-enters the retry schedule.

openapiOps.summary: Publish a creator signed collection manifest
openapiOps.description: The manifest is verified structurally, the creator signature address is bound, and the membership root is recomputed before publication. A published manifest is immutable; corrections are new versions.

openapiOps.summary: List published manifests
openapiOps.description: Keyset paginated, filterable by collection id, network, and status.

openapiOps.summary: One collection manifest
openapiOps.description: Superseded and revoked versions stay visible; history is never deleted.

parameters.name: manifestId
parameters.description: The manifest digest or its published identifier.

openapiOps.summary: A membership proof for one member
openapiOps.description: The SDK verifies the proof offline with nothing but this response.

openapiOps.summary: Supersede or revoke a manifest
openapiOps.description: Both moves are creator signed. A revocation does not delete history.

parameters.name: manifestId
parameters.description: The manifest the revision applies to.

openapiOps.summary: The full provenance record of a collection
openapiOps.description: Separate labels for the cryptographic claim, the on chain anchor, Universe curation, third party curation, and community reports.

openapiOps.summary: Whether the Counterparty authority currently proves ownership
openapiOps.description: The heritage market fails closed unless the self hosted Counterparty Core is ready, fresh, and on the intended network. There is no public API fallback in production.

openapiOps.summary: One Counterparty asset with its live attachment state
openapiOps.description: Identity is the authoritative numeric asset id plus current ledger state. A ticker or name alone is never an identity.

parameters.name: assetId
parameters.description: The numeric Counterparty asset id or its exact long name.

openapiOps.summary: The UTXOs currently carrying an asset
openapiOps.description: Each record binds quantity, outpoint, and the authority checkpoints it was read at.

parameters.name: assetId
parameters.description: The numeric Counterparty asset id or its exact long name.

openapiOps.summary: The Counterparty assets of one address
openapiOps.description: Address balances and their current attached outpoints.

openapiOps.summary: Compose a user signed attach transaction
openapiOps.description: Returns the unsigned PSBT, the exact XCP gas and miner fee, and everything that would travel. The user signs with their own wallet; the server never holds the asset, XCP, or BTC.

openapiOps.summary: Compose a user signed detach transaction
openapiOps.description: The same guarantees as attach, in reverse.

openapiOps.summary: Open an offline signing session
openapiOps.description: Creates the expected transaction manifest for one prepared transaction and returns it for review, export, or QR animation.

openapiOps.summary: List your signing sessions
openapiOps.description: Sessions of the authenticated account, newest first.

openapiOps.summary: One signing session
openapiOps.description: Includes the manifest, the imported signed result, and any rejection with its stable code.

openapiOps.summary: Import a signed result for verification
openapiOps.description: The signed result is compared against the manifest. Any change to the unsigned transaction, its outputs, the fee bound, or the asset destinations refuses the import with a stable code.

openapiOps.summary: Verify a manifest and signed result pair without a session
openapiOps.description: The same checks the session flow runs, usable directly by SDK consumers and the reference conformance tests.

asyncapiChannels.name: eventsStream
asyncapiChannels.description: Server sent events. The SSE id field carries the event id; sending Last-Event-ID resumes exactly after it. Filters: network, type, aggregateType, aggregateId, protocol, collectionId.

heartbeat.description: A comment line at least every 15 seconds so proxies never close an idle stream.

asyncapiChannels.name: eventsSocket
asyncapiChannels.description: WebSocket for high volume consumers. One connection, many subscriptions, cursor resumption, bounded buffers, slow consumer disconnect with a resumable cursor.

cursor.description: Resume from this event sequence and id.

subscribe.description: Multiplex many filters over one connection.

asyncapiChannels.name: webhookDelivery
